title: Open-Source Scheming-in-the-Wild Lite: A Transcript Triage Classifier

original_idea.body:
# Open-Source Scheming-in-the-Wild Lite: A Transcript Triage Classifier

**Problem:** A 2026 paper detected 698 real-world scheming incidents from 183k public transcripts, showing transcript-based OSINT is viable for scheming detection. But it relied on heavy pipelines; a lightweight, reproducible triage classifier that small teams could run is missing.

**Direction:** Assemble a small labeled set of public AI-agent transcripts (clearly-scheming-flagged vs. benign, from the paper's categories or public dumps). Train a cheap classifier (embedding + logistic regression, plus an LLM-judge baseline) for first-pass triage and report precision/recall and the false-positive burden at scale.

**Why it matters:** Scalable real-world scheming surveillance is strategically valuable and inherently lab-independent (uses public data). A cheap, open triage tool lowers the barrier for community monitoring of deployed-agent misbehavior.

**Relevant context:** Extends 'Scheming in the wild: detecting real-world AI scheming incidents with open-source intelligence' (arXiv:2604.09104, 2026), which analyzed 183,420 transcripts and found 698 incidents (Oct 2025-Mar 2026).
